claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 3 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 3 years old and lives with you at home.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that - my living situation is a bit complicated at the moment and I'm not certain how to answer that question.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand that living situations can be complicated. Let me ask this in a different way to help clarify:

Where are you physically residing most of the time right now? Are you in the UK, or are you living in another country?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: To be honest, I really can't say for certain. My situation is quite unclear right now, and I don't know how to categorize where I'm living.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it sounds like your living situation is genuinely uncertain at the moment.

Let me ask about another aspect of your situation: Are you the person who is responsible for Alex's day-to-day care? For example, are you the one providing for his food, clothes, and other needs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm the one looking after Alex day-to-day - I take care of all his needs, his food, clothes, everything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful to know.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation, or does he live at home with you full-time?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He lives at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's good to know, thank you.

Just a few more questions:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One more question: Does Alex have any connection to the UK - for example, was he born in the UK, is he a UK citizen, or does he have any immigration status in the UK (such as settled or pre-settled status)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about those details - I don't have that information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask one final question to help complete my assessment:

Do you yourself have any connection to the UK - such as being a UK citizen, having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or being a Crown servant working abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't know - I'm not sure about my status in that regard.

Since you're unable to confirm whether you currently live in the UK, and you don't have information about your own UK status (such as citizenship or immigration status) or Alex's connection to the UK, I cannot determine whether you meet this essential requirement.

To move forward with a Child Benefit claim, you would need to clarify your residency situation and your UK status. If you're unsure about these matters, you may want to contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly, who can discuss your specific circumstances and help determine your eligibility. They can be reached through the contact details on the gov.uk website.
